checks: The barycentric coordinate bounds are pointwise on the full bodies: at A only cap i is present, at B only j, and at M both i and j. In the extremal dimension d=2 the strict choice δ<t makes (1−δ)/2>t; all other coordinates are at most δ<t in every d≥2.

The hull projection is the entire stated rectangle. At second coordinate zero, only the bottom endpoint generators contribute, so all three bottom fibers are the stated Minkowski sections. At integer second coordinates 1, 2 or 3 the full D is present, and convexity in D excludes any extra continuous points. All actual sampled volumes are positive.

The three bottom bodies are translates of δD, so their physical surface masses are equal and the common translated facet normals agree almost everywhere. The translated swap pairs matching physical facet points and its midpoint measure is exactly 2μ_M, with full selected load 2s(ω_i+ω_j).

For any self-coupling, equality of both endpoint marginals forces equal crossflows r. All midpoint outputs remain in the actual corresponding convex fibers, even before imposing support on the boundaries. Physical domination forces 2r≤s at M, and the pointwise cap classifications make the load exactly (s+r)(ω_i+ω_j). This uses coefficient-one actual capacity, not original volume or a stationarity constraint.

The half-diagonal, half-swap pairing gives midpoint measure μ_A/2+μ_M+μ_B/2. It is dominated also on the marked normal bundle because each part carries its actual facet marks. Jensen in the full physical coordinates, including the base, gives 2μ_M≤_cxμ_A+μ_B and therefore the claimed convex-order improvement.

The selected hinge difference is t−δλ_i(ξ), computed using the strict endpoint and midpoint incidences. It stays positive including on all facets. Exact rational checks in d=2–20 confirmed the strict cutoff inequalities, hinge difference and optimal factor 3/4.
The source digest and §§1–3 match the actual hull, same marginals and sharp lost load. Its statement is an obstruction for this auxiliary capacity regime, not a counterexample to mixed-integer depth.

overlap.comparison: Repairs old normal-preserving physical support pairs under a 2^n surface-capacity ceiling. It neither asserts coefficient-one global domination nor preservation of the old nonconvex cap load. The example uses n=2 and hence does not contradict that ceiling.

Preserves separately specified endpoint crossflow measures from a three-fiber martingale and uses one branch’s mass for the midpoint law. This example has unrestricted self-coupling with identical endpoint-aggregate marginals and counts both symmetric crossflows, so the capacity and cap-load statements do not coincide.

Supplies normal-preserving martingales between prescribed convex-ordered boundary measures. It does not realize a given measure as a midpoint distribution of a self-coupling with this common marginal, nor control its selected cap load.

readability: The final strict-convexity comparison means that switching the coupling to the full diagonal law strictly increases the integral if the original coupling assigns positive mass to pairs with unequal physical coordinates.
